title: Weighted scores and constraints
goals: Explain how weight choices change outcomes

prerequisite.prompt: Which is closer under absolute-gap distance: a gap of 2 or a gap of 5?

vocabulary: A multiplier expressing the importance assigned to a feature
A number calculated to compare options
A requirement an option must meet
Improving one preference while giving up another

blocks.text: A fictional activity chooser uses enjoyment and learning ratings from 0 to 5. Its score is 2 times enjoyment plus learning. The activity must also take at most 20 minutes. Duration is a hard requirement; a high score cannot compensate for exceeding it.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: Only A is printed, with score 10. If B took 20 minutes it would qualify and have the higher score 11. The inclusive boundary matters. Ratings and weights are invented for practice and require justification before use in a real decision.

blocks.label: If enjoyment weight becomes 1 and learning weight becomes 2, find both scores before applying the same duration limit.

blocks.text: Choosing the highest score and only then ignoring its duration breaks the requirement. Filter for eligibility first. If no item qualifies, report no eligible option instead of relaxing a requirement silently.

Weights represent preferences, not a discovered truth. Explain who chose them and test whether small changes alter the recommendation. Avoid claiming that a larger score proves greater educational value.

blocks.label: For eligible A (fun 4, learning 1) and B (fun 2, learning 4), compare weights (2,1) with (1,2).

workbook.title: Calculate a score
workbook.prompt: An eligible activity has fun 2 and learning 4. Use 2 * fun + learning.

workbook.title: Check a boundary
workbook.prompt: Which durations 19, 20, 21 qualify under at most 20?

workbook.title: Repair selection
workbook.prompt: An ineligible item scores 15 and an eligible item scores 9. Which should be offered under the stated policy?
workbook.answer: Offer the eligible item with score 9. The constraint is applied before ranking.

workbook.title: Choose independently
workbook.prompt: Limit is 15 minutes. A has fun 3, learning 4, minutes 15; B has 5, 1, 16; C has 2, 5, 12. Calculate scores with 2 * fun + learning and choose.
workbook.answer: Scores A 10, B 11, C 9. B is excluded. A is highest among eligible options.

workbook.title: Test sensitivity
workbook.prompt: For eligible A (fun 4, learning 1) and B (fun 2, learning 4), compare weights (2,1) with (1,2).
workbook.answer: First scores A 9, B 8 so A wins. Second scores A 6, B 10 so B wins. Explain the preference change.

teacher.background: Teach Week 23 as a two-session investigation using fictional data. A fictional activity chooser uses enjoyment and learning ratings from 0 to 5. Its score is 2 times enjoyment plus learning. The activity must also take at most 20 minutes. Duration is a hard requirement; a high score cannot compensate for exceeding it. Assess the three stated outcomes through the independent task, not by copying the worked result.

Paper trace table and the student workbook
Fictional input records from this lesson; no real student identifiers
